stories.title: PwC India opens AI lab in Gurugram
stories.summary: PwC India has launched a Future AI Experience Lab in Gurugram to help businesses explore AI and move toward business impact. The facility aims to assist leaders with questions on where to invest and how to govern as the conversation shifts toward autonomous agents and physical AI.

stories.title: PwC India lab offers 90 AI solutions
stories.summary: PwC India's new Gurugram facility houses over 90 industry-specific AI solutions, including robotics and agentic AI. The lab is designed to help businesses simulate operations and test applications across sectors such as manufacturing, infrastructure, and pharmaceuticals. The space is now open for operational experimentation.

stories.title: Deloitte links AI to cyberattack surge
stories.summary: Deloitte India reports a 1,200 percent surge in AI-driven cyberattacks, noting that static risk assessment methods are failing to keep pace. The firm urges insurers to adopt intelligence-led underwriting that incorporates real-time threat data and behavioural metrics to maintain accurate coverage in a volatile environment.

stories.title: Sarvam AI seeks Deloitte partnership
stories.summary: Nvidia-backed Sarvam AI is reportedly looking to partner with Deloitte to expand enterprise adoption of its products. The move aims to translate investor backing into commercial deployments as the global AI market faces increased scrutiny over valuations and spending. Deloitte would provide advisory and implementation services.

stories.title: Deloitte calls for intelligence-led insurance
stories.summary: Deloitte India says traditional cyber risk assessments are inadequate against AI-driven attacks and expanding digital ecosystems. The report argues that insurers must move toward real-time threat intelligence and continuous monitoring, as historical loss data no longer provides a sufficient basis for evaluating modern cyber exposure.

stories.title: EY Han Young acquires 2e Consulting
stories.summary: EY Han Young is acquiring IT firm 2e Consulting to strengthen its AI transformation advisory business. The deal adds three decades of experience in financial and public-sector IT projects to the firm's capabilities. The purchase price was not disclosed, and the acquisition is expected to bolster cybersecurity services.

stories.title: EY Han Young buys ToYou Consulting
stories.summary: Global firm EY Han Young has signed an agreement to acquire ToYou Consulting, a Korean firm specializing in digital and IT services. The move is intended to expand the company's presence in the financial and public-sector markets. The strategic investment aims to enhance services for the AI era.

stories.title: Qantas partners with Accenture for tech overhaul
stories.summary: Qantas has entered a multi-year partnership with Accenture to replace legacy systems and accelerate its use of artificial intelligence. The airline is focusing on modernizing its technology stack as it manages fuel costs and capacity settings in a competitive market environment.

stories.title: Tech services M&A activity rises
stories.summary: Technology services mergers and acquisitions rose 4.7 percent to 247 deals in the third quarter, with a total value of $5.3 billion. EY reports that buyers are prioritizing data foundations and AI-native services to move artificial intelligence from experimentation to deployment in complex enterprise environments.

stories.title: Cyber insurance market faces AI threat
stories.summary: Deloitte India projects the domestic cyber insurance market will reach $594 million by fiscal year 2031. The report warns that static risk models are failing against dynamic AI-driven threats, necessitating a shift toward intelligence-led underwriting to strengthen economic resilience as attack surfaces continue to expand.

stories.title: Cyber insurance demand grows in India
stories.summary: Deloitte India expects the cyber insurance market to reach up to $594 million by fiscal year 2031, driven by digital adoption and rising cyber incidents. The report notes that insurers' digital expansion has outpaced their resilience and suggests moving beyond questionnaire-based assessments to manage third-party risks.

stories.title: KPMG CEO outlook focuses on AI value
stories.summary: KPMG's 2026 CEO Outlook suggests that retail leaders are shifting focus from whether to transform to where transformation creates the most value. As AI becomes embedded in the customer journey, executives are balancing near-term pressures with long-term ambitions to enhance decision-making and workforce capabilities.

stories.title: Bain warns retailers on AI search visibility
stories.summary: Bain & Company research suggests that market share no longer guarantees retailers visibility in AI shopping answers. The report analyzed 4,400 shopping prompts and found that retailers absent from AI search results risk losing traffic and profits as consumers increasingly rely on personal agents for purchase recommendations.

stories.title: McKinsey report highlights supply chain risks
stories.summary: A new McKinsey report finds that about a quarter of global imports face serious supply risks, with critical products like semiconductors and oil being the most exposed. The study notes that China supplies 31 percent of the most vulnerable US imports, while the US supplies 8 percent of China's.

stories.title: India needs $400 billion for steel target
stories.summary: McKinsey reports that India requires up to $400 billion in investment to reach its target of 600 million tonnes of annual steelmaking capacity by 2047. While capacity reached 233 million tonnes in fiscal year 2026, about half of the required volume for future targets has not started construction.

stories.title: McKinsey sees value shift in physical AI
stories.summary: McKinsey now estimates physical AI will generate over $1 trillion in value by 2035. The firm expects value to shift from robot hardware makers to software, deployment, and field operations, placing the buyer's site and operational data at the center of future physical AI investments.

stories.title: CII-BCG report projects machinery market growth
stories.summary: A report by the CII and Boston Consulting Group projects India's capital goods market could reach $1.2 trillion by 2047. Growth is expected to be driven by domestic manufacturing ambitions in AI, semiconductors, defense, and renewable energy as the country works to reduce its reliance on imports.

stories.title: Capital goods market growth forecast
stories.summary: The CII and Boston Consulting Group project India's capital goods market will grow to $1.2 trillion by 2047. Annual capital expenditure in data centers and semiconductors is expected to quadruple by fiscal year 2029, making it the fastest-growing segment within the broader machinery manufacturing industry.

stories.title: Adani Energy Solutions acquires Vikramshila Power Transmission
stories.summary: Adani Energy Solutions has signed an agreement to acquire 100% of Vikramshila Power Transmission, the special purpose vehicle for a transmission project in Bihar. The infrastructure is intended to evacuate power from the 2,400 MW Pirpainti thermal plant. The company expects the acquisition to remain in focus.

stories.title: Adani Energy Solutions Acquires Vikramshila Power Transmission for Bihar Project, Shares Rise 0.88% - HDFC Sky
Cross-border M&A activity rises 31 percent
stories.summary: Global M&A activity is up 31% this year according to Oliver Wyman, as dealmakers navigate geopolitical uncertainty. The industry is on course for its biggest year since 2021. After several fallow years, the market has turned a corner toward a record year for cross-border dealmaking.

stories.title: Oliver Wyman to acquire Synpulse
stories.summary: Oliver Wyman has agreed to acquire financial services and technology consultancy Synpulse. The transaction is expected to close in early 2027, with terms undisclosed. The deal adds 1,200 employees and technology expertise to the Marsh & McLennan consulting business. The acquisition was announced on November 19.

stories.title: Oliver Wyman expands AI capabilities with Synpulse acquisition
stories.summary: Oliver Wyman has agreed to acquire Synpulse to integrate its AI engineering and technology platform. The firms have already collaborated on client transformation projects. The deal is expected to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. Financial institutions are adapting to advances in technology and AI.

stories.title: Teneo hires Mike Granowski for energy practice
stories.summary: Teneo has hired Mike Granowski as a senior managing director in its energy and infrastructure practice. Based in Chicago, Granowski will focus on nuclear energy and the power sector. He brings 25 years of experience in strategy, transactions, and capital programs to the management consulting firm.

stories.title: Oliver Wyman to acquire Synpulse
stories.summary: Oliver Wyman has agreed to acquire Synpulse, a technology consultancy serving banks and insurers. The firm, founded in 1996, employs 1,200 people. The acquisition aims to provide more capacity for replacing legacy systems and AI engineering. The deal is expected to close in early 2027.

stories.title: Oliver Wyman to buy Synpulse in AI push
stories.summary: Oliver Wyman has agreed to acquire technology and AI platform company Synpulse. The firms have already worked together on end-to-end client transformations. The deal is expected to close in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. Terms were not disclosed. Clients are seeking partners to navigate technology and AI.

stories.title: Rosely Group buys adtech PR agency The Digital Voice in seven-figure deal - Dealroom
AI threats push India cyber insurance toward smarter underwriting
stories.summary: A Deloitte report notes a 1,200% surge in AI-driven phishing is forcing India's cyber insurance market to adopt intelligence-led underwriting. Traditional risk assessment methods are struggling to keep pace with automated digital threats. The industry is moving toward more sophisticated models to address the evolving landscape.

stories.title: Pharma GCCs in India generate 10.5 billion dollars
stories.summary: India's pharma global capability centres generate 10.5 billion dollars in gross value added and employ 120,000 professionals, according to an OPPI-EY report. These centres are moving beyond support roles to take on global mandates across science and technology. Most top biopharma companies now operate centres in India.

stories.title: Kolkata emerges as new GCC hotspot
stories.summary: Kolkata saw a 239% year-on-year growth in GCC gross leasing volume in 2025, reaching 0.5 million sqft. EY India notes the city is emerging as a complement to Tier-1 hubs. Indian GCCs are shifting from cost-focused models to research and value-driven centres as technology and talent advance.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh promotes Amaravati Economic Region
stories.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government is developing the Amaravati Economic Region as a major growth engine. The region covers 27% of the state and accounts for 35% of its gross state domestic product. The master plan includes nine districts, five of which are among the state's richest.

stories.title: Adani Energy wins transmission project for Bihar plant
stories.summary: Adani Energy Solutions has secured a transmission project linked to the 2,400 MW Pirpainti thermal plant. The company signed a share purchase agreement to acquire 100% equity in Vikramshila Power Transmission. The acquisition will be made through a cash consideration for the special-purpose vehicle.

stories.title: Manufacturing sector drives self-reliance in India
stories.summary: India's manufacturing sector has been reshaped by reforms under the Make in India vision over the past 12 years. Government initiatives like the Production Linked Incentive scheme and PM GatiShakti aim to accelerate production of defence, medical devices, and electronics for domestic and international markets.

stories.title: Google to invest 5 million dollars in IIT Kharagpur
stories.summary: Google will invest 5 million dollars in IIT Kharagpur to support AI research. The funding targets development in Indic languages, materials science, and agriculture. The company aims to help the institution deploy AI models to tackle real-world problems through its research and student programs.

stories.title: Maharashtra urged to plan land acquisition in advance
stories.summary: NITI Aayog has advised Maharashtra to formulate a long-term land acquisition policy for future development. Officials suggested acquiring land at current prices to avoid higher costs later. The state is reviewing its development projects and infrastructure needs to ensure proper management of future land requirements.

stories.title: India capital goods market projected to reach 1.2 trillion dollars
stories.summary: India's capital goods market could reach 1.2 trillion dollars by 2047, according to a CII and BCG report. Investments in data centres and semiconductors are expected to drive demand for machinery. Annual capital expenditure in these segments is projected to quadruple by 2029.

SPJIMR team wins EY-Parthenon contest
PwC India chairperson on hiring fresh graduates
stories.summary: Sanjeev Krishan, chairperson of PwC in India, says companies must bridge the gap between education and employment. He suggests the government's apprenticeship initiative and increased job creation are necessary to support young talent. The firm is currently working with colleges to improve industry-ready skills for new graduates.

stories.title: Campus recruitment remains central to Indian hiring
stories.summary: Thousands of graduates enter the workforce annually through organised campus recruitment programmes. Companies across sectors including consulting, financial services, and information technology participate in these drives to identify talent. The ecosystem remains a primary method for institutions to transition students into the professional job market.

stories.title: Gen Z employees and workplace leave
stories.summary: Research suggests Gen Z employees often prefer honesty when requesting time off to avoid the mental effort of lying. While some studies indicate that avoiding deceit reduces stress and guilt, data shows that workplace honesty remains inconsistent across the generation. Lying is described as hard work for the brain.

stories.title: PwC India chief on shifting job market demands
stories.summary: Sanjeev Krishan, chairperson of PwC in India, says companies now prioritise professionals who deliver measurable business outcomes. With demand rising for specialised skills in data science and technology, the firm hires 3,500 to 4,000 people annually. Clients are increasingly paying for results rather than hours worked.

stories.title: PwC India chief says experience is a necessity
stories.summary: PwC India chairperson Sanjeev Krishan says jobs are available, but employers now demand relevant experience to drive business growth. As business requirements evolve, specialised skills have become a key hiring priority. Experience is now framed as a necessity for those entering the current job market.

stories.title: Campus Spotlight: Griffin Mascia - Alvarez & Marsal
Campus offers rise for class of 2027
stories.summary: Top offers for the class of 2027 reached 32 lakh per annum at SRCC and LSR. While average salaries increased, the total number of offers at SRCC dipped to 190 from 213. Top consulting firms returned to campus, though some previous high-paying recruiters did not visit this year.
